why.simple: This record can only spot changes bigger than a typical one.
why.scientific: MDT ≈ 0.61 °C/decade over 19.3 yr vs expected 0.20 (≈0.2 °C per decade, global mean surface warming since the 1970s (NASA GISS)): not detectable.

text.simple: Another instrument shows the same direction, but is not sure yet.
text.scientific: Overlapping window 2002-09 to 2021-12, same place, each series de-seasonalised over that window. AIRS (Surface air temperature (daytime, AIRS ascending)): -0.454 °C per decade, p = 0.0127. MERRA-2 (2-m air temperature (NASA POWER, MERRA-2-based)): -0.263 °C per decade, p = 0.32 (p is the weaker of the two decisive tests). Same sign, but only one is significant at 0.05. AIRS is a snapshot at about 1:30 (day or night pass), the other series is a daily mean: compare the direction only, not the size. The grid cells differ (1.0° vs 0.5°), so the footprints differ.

text.simple: The two instruments do not tell the same story yet.
text.scientific: Overlapping window 2002-09 to 2021-12, same place, each series de-seasonalised over that window. AIRS (Surface air temperature (night-time, AIRS descending)): +0.243 °C per decade, p = 0.0441. MERRA-2 (2-m air temperature (NASA POWER, MERRA-2-based)): -0.263 °C per decade, p = 0.32 (p is the weaker of the two decisive tests). Neither is significant at 0.05 together with the same sign, so there is no contrast to report. AIRS is a snapshot at about 1:30 (day or night pass), the other series is a daily mean: compare the direction only, not the size. The grid cells differ (1.0° vs 0.5°), so the footprints differ.
